name: Why is scribe molding necessary on kitchen cabinets?

mainEntity.name: Why is scribe molding necessary on kitchen cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Molding covers the natural expansion gaps and minor leveling discrepancies that occur where cabinetry meets drywall. Walls and ceilings are rarely plumb or square, especially in older residences. Scribe molding conceals gaps along side panels, baseboards bridge the transition between flooring and walls, and crown molding masks shifting ceiling heights. A finish contractor uses these profiles to turn standard modular cabinetry into a cohesive, architectural installation. Without molding, uneven gaps along drywall and cut cabinet edges remain exposed, allowing dust and debris to accumulate in hard-to-reach pockets.
acceptedAnswer.description: Scribe molding is a thin, flexible trim piece that covers uneven gaps between cabinet edges and wavy drywall walls, creating a clean, flush appearance.
